answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake bonds to audit peer transaction graphs. Verifiers search for topological cuts isolating synthetic clusters, creating an impassable canyon between honest nodes and fraudulent clusters. Auditing committee cross-validation provides crystal clarity on coordinated behavior; detecting collusion triggers stake slashing. A verified agent's historical state acts as a non-transferable relic, forcing attacker costs to scale superlinearly with graph density.
